prompt: Pull the @param, @return and @throws tags out of a Javadoc comment given as a String. Complete the three DocTagExtractor methods and run the tests.
explanation: Javadoc tags live at the start of a cleaned line, so the whole job is: normalise each line, test for the tag, then take the first word after it. Writing one private helper that takes the tag name keeps @param, @throws and @exception from turning into three near-identical loops. Note that the order of the returned names matters -- callers use it to match tags against a parameter list.
hints: Split the comment on "\n" and clean each line before testing it: trim, remove a leading "/**" or "*", then trim again.
A tag line starts with the tag followed by a space; the name you want is the first word of whatever follows.
Write one private helper that collects the names after a given tag, then call it with "@param", "@throws" and "@exception".
